walkthroughs.body_html:
A force is just a push or a pull.

You feel forces every day — kicking a ball, opening a door, even sitting on a chair. Forces can be contact (like friction) or non-contact (like gravity).

We measure forces in newtons (N). One newton is roughly the weight of a small apple. 🍎

Mass is how much stuff is in an object. It's in kilograms (kg) and never changes.

Weight is the pull of gravity on that mass. It's a force, so it's in newtons (N).

On Earth, gravity pulls with about g = 10 N/kg. So a 1 kg bag of sugar weighs about 10 N.

When more than one force acts on an object, we add them up to get the resultant force.

If you push a box right with 8 N and friction pulls left with 3 N, the resultant is 5 N to the right.

If the resultant is zero, the object is balanced — it stays still or keeps moving at the same speed.

mcqs.q: Which of these is a force?
options: Mass
Friction
Time
Volume

mcqs.q: What unit do we measure force in?
options: Kilograms
Newtons
Joules
Metres

mcqs.q: If an object is moving at constant velocity in a straight line, what is the net force on it?
options: Zero — by Newton's first law, constant velocity requires zero net force.
There must be a forward force on the object to keep it moving.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between mass and weight?
options: Mass is the amount of matter (kg); weight is the gravitational force on that mass (N) and depends on g.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
The net force equals the velocity times the mass of the object.
Mass and weight are the same thing, just expressed in different units.

mcqs.q: If air resistance is ignored, which falls faster: a heavy ball or a light ball dropped from the same height?
options: Both fall at the same rate because gravitational acceleration is independent of mass.
Heavier objects fall faster than lighter objects because gravity pulls more on them.
The lighter ball falls faster because it has less inertia.
Mass changes with location but weight does not.
